newsitem.title: USA: Rubin warns against proclaiming new inflation era.
newsitem.headline: Rubin warns against proclaiming new inflation era.

text.p: The economy's stunning recent performance is no guarantee it has entered a "new era" in which faster growth might be possible without higher inflation, said Treasury Secretary Robert Rubin.

Rubin conceded he had no answer to a question on the likelihood that productivity improvements and technological advances had boosted the maximum sustainable, non-inflationary growth rate in the United States.

"I've always remained very watchful and very skeptical about the notion that somehow or other we're in a new era of wonderful conditions with respect to inflation," in response to a question from the audience after a speech to a meeting of the Investment Company Institute.

"Having said all that, ... when you look out there, it is a little hard to see, at least for me, any indication of a resurgence of inflation. So i guess my view of this is to say that I don't know the answer," said Rubin.

The Treasury chief added that he considered the question highly important, and that he had asked it of candidates for the Federal Reserve Board of Governors in the past and that it arose among global finance officials as recently as the April 27 International Monetary Fund meetings.
"It may be the single most important question with respect to the economic outlook," he said.

"I guess my view is, from a policy point-of-view, that what we ought to do is to pursue policies that will give us as much growth as we can with low inflation, but always to remain very watchful, because I think there's no way of knowing at this point, other than to say that there have been many times before when people thought we entered new eras of one sort or another and then found out that they were transitory," Rubin added.
